phrase: The hungry alligator eats the bigger number.
exception: Open mouth faces the larger value. Compare the numbers first — do not memorize left/right shapes alone.
steps: Draw < or > as an open mouth.
Point the open side at the greater number.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Put the big number in your head, then count on.
exception: Inefficient for large addends; may encourage counting by ones forever.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Make a ten, then add the rest.
exception: Needs solid number-bond fluency.
steps: Split one addend to complete a ten.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Doubles plus one: double the small number, then add one more.
exception: Students sometimes double the larger number instead.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Even numbers share fair: everyone gets a buddy. Odd numbers leave one out.
exception: Confuses with divisible-by-2 for large numbers if pairing is skipped.
steps: Even: no leftover; odd: one leftover.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Five or more, raise the score. Four or less, let it rest.
exception: School rule: 5 or more raises the digit. Carry through 9s (1.96→2.0 at 1 d.p.). Banker's rounding differs and is usually not school policy.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: Hour is a short word: short hand. Minute is a long word: long hand.
exception: Digital clocks and 24-hour time break the metaphor.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: More on top? No need to stop. More on the floor? Go next door and get ten more.
exception: Never flip digits to subtract smaller from larger. Borrow carefully across zeros. 52−27 is 25, not 35.
steps: If bottom larger, borrow ten from next place.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Ten ones make a ten. Carry the one next door.
exception: Students carry without writing the ones digit.
steps: If 10+, write ones digit and carry a ten.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Knuckles are 31-day months; valleys between are shorter.
exception: February is 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. After July continue onto the other fist at August.
reason: Reliable calendar aid with leap-year exception.

phrase: Thirty days hath September, April, June, and November.
exception: All the rest have 31, except February (28, or 29 in a leap year).
reason: Traditional accurate calendar fact.

phrase: Times means groups of.
exception: Order language can confuse commutative property.
steps: Read a×b as a groups of b.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Fold the finger for ×9. Left fingers are tens; right are ones.
exception: Works for 9×1 through 9×10. For larger factors use 10n−n.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Five, six, seven, eight: fifty-six is seven times eight.
exception: Only helps one fact.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Long division loop: Divide, Multiply, Subtract, Bring down (repeat).
exception: Place value matters. Remainder must be < divisor. Chant ≠ understanding remainders as fractions/decimals.
reason: Algorithm reminder only if place value is taught.

phrase: 2–5–10: last digit. 3–9: digit sum. 4–8: last 2/3 digits. 11: alternating sum. 6: both 2 and 3.
exception: Omits a clean rule for 7. Digit sum for 9 is repeated until small. Alternating sum for 11 may be 0.
reason: Rules are correct; original chant omitted 6 and overclaimed completeness.

phrase: Perimeter is the fence around. Area is the carpet inside.
exception: Students still swap formulas under time pressure.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: What you do to the top, you do to the bottom.
exception: Multiply or divide top and bottom by the same nonzero number. Never 'do the same' when adding fractions.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: Fives are half of tens — and they end in 0 or 5.
exception: Half-of-tens fails for odd multiples if students forget halves.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: ×2 is double. ×4 is double-double. ×8 is double-double-double.
exception: One double ×2; two doubles ×4; three doubles ×8. Stopping early halves the answer.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: For ×11: split the digits and park their sum in the middle.
exception: If the middle sum ≥10, carry 1 to the left digit.
steps: Write digit sum in middle (carry if ≥10).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Please Excuse My Dear Aunt Sally — but ×÷ tie and +− tie, left to right.
exception: × and ÷ are the same level (left to right): 8 ÷ 2 × 4 = 16, not 1. Same for + and −. Grouping includes brackets, fraction bars, and | | — not only parentheses.
reason: Classic acronym usable only if left-to-right ties are taught; letter order alone is a known trap.

phrase: BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, then ÷ and × together, then + and − together.
exception: Division is not before multiplication — shared precedence, left to right. Same for +/−. 'Orders' means powers and roots.
reason: Sound Commonwealth variant; must fix the D-before-M myth.

phrase: BEDMAS: Brackets, Exponents, then ÷ and × together, then + and − together.
exception: Do not do all division before multiplication. Work × and ÷ left to right; + and − left to right.
reason: Canadian variant; needs the tie-level exception. Concept already covered by PEMDAS/BODMAS in-app.

phrase: GEMS: Grouping, Exponents, Multiply/Divide, Subtract/Add.
exception: Within Multiply/Divide and within Subtract/Add, still go left to right. Grouping includes ( ), [ ], { }, fraction bars, and | |.
reason: Pairs operations correctly in the acronym itself; clearest order-of-operations family member.

phrase: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the second fraction.
exception: Flip only the second fraction. Convert mixed numbers first. Never divide by zero.
reason: Correct as multiplying by the reciprocal; bare three-word chant is overgeneralized.

phrase: Same bottom, add the tops.
exception: Only when denominators already match. Do not add denominators.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Straight across: tops times tops, bottoms times bottoms.
exception: Denominators need not match for ×. 1/2×1/2=1/4, not 1.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Numerator up, denominator down.
exception: Names parts only — does not tell you how to operate on fractions.
reason: True vocabulary mnemonic.

phrase: Mixed → improper: Multiply whole × denominator, Add numerator, Denominator stays.
exception: Denominator never changes. Multiply by the bottom, not the top. 2 3/4 = 11/4, not 11/8.
reason: Procedure correct; MAD alone needs a strong Watch out.

phrase: Line up the dots.
exception: Students right-align like whole numbers.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Ignore the dots, multiply, then count the places back in.
exception: Trailing zeros and place-count errors.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Make the divisor whole: hop both dots the same number of places.
exception: Move both decimal points the same number of places so the divisor is whole. Unequal hops change the quotient.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: King Henry Died By Drinking Chocolate Milk — Kilo, Hecto, Deca, Base, Deci, Centi, Milli.
exception: 'By' is the base unit. Mega/micro/nano are off this ladder. Each step is ×10 or ÷10.
reason: Standard metric ladder; must teach Base and off-ladder prefixes.

phrase: Hey diddle diddle, the median's the middle; you add and divide for the mean. The mode is the most, and the range is the difference between.
exception: Sort before the median. Even n → average of two middles. Multimodal / no mode possible. Range = max − min.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Mode and most share letters — mode is the most frequent value.
exception: A data set can have no mode or more than one mode.
reason: Sound definition hook.

phrase: The median is the middle value — like a median strip in the road.
exception: Sort first. If n is even, average the two middle values.
steps: Even n → average of two middles
reason: Good definition mnemonic with even-n exception.

phrase: For × and ÷ of signs: same signs positive, different signs negative.
exception: Applies only to multiplication and division — never to addition or subtraction.
reason: Friend/enemy metaphor is easily over-applied to addition; rephrase to the sign rule.

phrase: Same signs are friends (positive product). Different signs are strangers (negative product).
exception: Only for × and ÷. For addition use absolute values and direction, not 'friends'.
reason: Metaphor OK for products/quotients if sharply limited.

phrase: I View Xylophones: I=1, V=5, X=10 (extend: L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000).
exception: Subtractive notation: IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900.
reason: Partial map; needs subtractive notation exception.

phrase: 5 tomatoes: 5,280 feet in a mile.
reason: Joke digit scaffold with no mathematical structure; easy to misremember.

phrase: A Rat In The House May Eat The Ice Cream.
reason: Spelling mnemonic for the word 'arithmetic', not a mathematical idea or procedure.

phrase: Commutative: order can commute — a+b=b+a and a×b=b×a.
exception: Subtraction and division are not commutative.
steps: Check if swapping operands keeps the same result
reason: Correct property mnemonic.

phrase: Associative: how you group (associate) does not change the sum or product.
exception: Not true for subtraction or division.
reason: Correct property mnemonic.

phrase: Distributive: give what's outside to every term inside the brackets.
exception: Distribute to every term, including signs: 2(x−3)=2x−6, not 2x−3.
steps: Multiply outside by each inside term
reason: Correct and high-value.

phrase: Dividend ÷ divisor = quotient (dividend is the amount being divided).
exception: In the 'house' diagram the dividend is inside; layouts vary. Remainder ≠ quotient.
reason: Vocabulary correct; 'at the end' depends on layout, so rephrased.

phrase: Same signs: add and keep. Different signs: subtract and keep the bigger one's sign.
exception: 'Bigger' means larger absolute value, not algebraically greater.
steps: Different → subtract; keep larger magnitude's sign.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Subtracting is adding the opposite: keep the first, change − to +, change the second number's sign.
exception: Only for subtraction → addition of the opposite. Do not apply to ×/÷. Do not confuse with Keep-Change-Flip.
reason: Correct if framed as adding the opposite; bare KCC is a known overgeneralization trap.

phrase: Per cent means out of 100. Hop the decimal two places.
exception: Percent means per 100. 10% of 10% is 1%, not 20%. More than 100% is allowed.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: I = PRT — I am pretty.
exception: Rate must match time unit; compound interest different.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: d = rt — dirt.
exception: Units must match. Average speed ≠ instantaneous speed.
reason: Simple true formula hook.

phrase: Distance = speed × time; cover up the unknown in the D–S–T relation.
exception: Use consistent units. Average speed is total distance ÷ total time — not the average of speeds.
reason: Formula triangle is a rearrangement aid; accept with unit/average-speed exceptions.

phrase: Do the opposite to both sides.
exception: Apply the inverse to every term on both sides. For inequalities, ×/÷ by a negative flips the inequality.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: Cherry pie's delicious: C = πd. Apple pies are too: A = πr².
exception: C=πd uses diameter; A=πr² uses radius. Halve a diameter before area. r² means r×r.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Apple pies are square: A = π r².
reason: Duplicate of the cherry/apple pie circle mnemonic; 'square' confuses area with a square shape.

phrase: What you want, over all you've got.
exception: Assumes equally likely outcomes. Compound events need care.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: For a proportion a/b = c/d, cross products are equal: a·d = b·c.
exception: Only when two ratios are equal. Never cross-multiply to add or multiply fractions. Keep units matched.
reason: Valid for proportions; butterfly drawing often misused on fraction addition.

phrase: New minus old, over old, times 100.
exception: Using new as denominator; successive percent changes.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Sale? Take it off. Tax? Put it on.
exception: Sale decreases; tax increases. Successive percents multiply.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Along the corridor, up the stairs.
exception: x first (along), then y (up/down).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Cover the floor, then stack the floors: length × width × height.
exception: Using slant height; unit cubes vs formula disconnect.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: A triangle is half the box: base × height ÷ 2.
exception: Use perpendicular height, not a slanted side. Parallelogram is base×height (no ÷2).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Slope is rise over run.
exception: Slope = rise/run. Horizontal → 0; vertical → undefined. Downward means negative rise.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: y = mx + b: Begin at b, then Move with m.
exception: b is the y-intercept (x=0). Rearrange into slope-intercept form first if needed. Vertical lines have no y=mx+b form.
steps: From there use rise/run from m
reason: Sound graphing hook for slope-intercept form.

phrase: Multiply → add powers. Divide → subtract. Power of a power → multiply.
exception: Different bases; negative exponents forgotten.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Negative exponent: take one over with a positive power.
exception: x^(−n)=1/x^n for x≠0. A negative exponent does not make the value negative by itself. 2^(−3)=1/8, not −8.
reason: Correct definition mnemonic.

phrase: One digit, then a dot, times a power of ten.
exception: Coefficient must satisfy 1 ≤ |a| < 10.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Square the legs, add them, and that is the long side squared.
exception: Using a non-hypotenuse as c; converse misuse.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Three corners make a straight line: 180°.
exception: Spherical geometry; exterior vs interior confusion.
steps: Interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Four corners make a full turn: 360°.
exception: Concave quads / complex polygons.
steps: Interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: F angles copy, Z angles copy, C angles make 180°.
exception: Mis-drawing F/Z/C on slanted diagrams.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Twin sides, twin angles.
exception: Equal sides face equal base angles.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Complementary = Corner (90°). Supplementary = Straight (180°).
exception: Angles need not share a ray — these are about measures, not necessarily adjacent diagrams.
reason: Correct definitions.

phrase: Acute is a 'cute' little angle — greater than 0° and less than 90°.
exception: Obtuse: (90°, 180°). Reflex: (180°, 360°). Right: exactly 90°.
reason: Harmless true vocabulary aid.

phrase: Scalene is the odd one out: no equal sides.
exception: Side names ≠ angle names (acute/right/obtuse).
reason: Correct classification hook.

phrase: Slide, flip, or turn: translation, reflection, rotation.
exception: Orientation/congruence after composition; glide reflections.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Cut the polygon into triangles: (n − 2) × 180°.
exception: Using exterior formula by mistake; regular vs irregular.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Walk around the shape: exterior angles always add to 360°.
exception: One exterior at each vertex, consistent orientation. Interior sum is (n−2)×180°.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: A cone is one-third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
exception: Same base radius and perpendicular height — not slant height.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Cylinder volume is the circle floor times the height: πr²h.
exception: Surface area formula mix-up.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Sphere volume: (4/3)πr³.
exception: Volume (4/3)πr³ vs surface 4πr². Halve a diameter before cubing.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: FOIL: First, Outside, Inside, Last — a checklist for two binomials.
exception: Only for (a+b)(c+d). Prefer distribute each-by-each. Watch signs. Longer polynomials need general distribution.
reason: Correct special case of distribution; not the definition of multiplying polynomials.

phrase: x equals negative b, plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, all over two a.
exception: If a=0 it is not quadratic. Δ<0 → no real roots. Divide the entire −b±√… by 2a.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).
exception: Trying a²+b² the same way.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.
exception: For x²+bx+c (a=1): two numbers multiply to c and add to b. If a≠1 use AC method or the formula.
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: Solve like an equation — but flip the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
exception: Only ×/÷ by a negative flips. Adding never flips. Swapping sides flips the symbol.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: flip the fraction and change the sign.
exception: Perpendicular ⇒ negative reciprocals. Horizontal ⊥ vertical.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: b² − 4ac: positive two, zero one, negative none (real roots).
exception: Δ>0 two distinct real roots; =0 repeated real root; <0 no real roots (complex conjugates exist).
reason: High-value mnemonic that is sound only with an explicit exception (common misuse).

phrase: STAR: Search, Translate, Answer, Review.
reason: Generic study heuristic, not a math mnemonic.

phrase: SOH CAH TOA.
exception: Wrong opposite/adjacent relative to reference angle.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Oscar Had A Heap Of Apples — Opposite/Hypotenuse, Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Opposite/Adjacent.
exception: Opposite/adjacent depend on the reference acute angle. Primary ratios are for right triangles.
reason: Equivalent to SOH CAH TOA; sound if order is taught.

phrase: All Students Take Calculus — Q1 all +, Q2 sin +, Q3 tan +, Q4 cos +.
exception: Different from CAST (starts in Q4). Reciprocals follow partner signs. Tan undefined where cos=0.
reason: Standard and correct with quadrant mapping made explicit.

phrase: CAST (from Quadrant IV, counterclockwise): Cos positive, All, Sin, Tan.
exception: Do not mix with ASTC (starts in Quadrant I). Reciprocals match their partner's sign.
reason: Correct if starting quadrant is explicit; easily confused with ASTC.

phrase: Cosec flips sine, sec flips cosine, cot flips tangent.
exception: csc=1/sin, sec=1/cos, cot=1/tan — not sec=1/sin.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; divide by cos² or sin² for the tan/cot forms.
exception: sin²θ means (sin θ)². sinθ+cosθ is not 1 — only the squares sum to 1. Square roots introduce ±.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: 'Co' means complement: sin(90°−θ)=cos θ.
exception: Using 180° instead of 90°; radian form π/2.
steps: Complementary angles swap sin↔cos, tan↔cot, sec↔csc.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Elevation looks up, depression looks down, both from the horizontal.
exception: Measuring from vertical; diagram orientation.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: On the unit circle: cosine is x, sine is y.
exception: Do not swap x/y. Signs follow the quadrant. Match calculator mode to the problem.
reason: Core true definition mnemonic.

phrase: May I have a large container of coffee? (3.1415926)
reason: Letter-count entertainment, not a classroom procedure; typos silently corrupt digits.

phrase: Same size and shape: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS.
exception: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS/HL work. SSA is not a congruence theorem (ambiguous case).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Bring the power down in front, then take one off the power.
exception: d/dx[x^n]=n x^(n−1). Composites need the chain rule.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: First d-second plus second d-first.
exception: Product rule is u'v+uv', not u'v'.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Low d-high minus high d-low, over the low squared.
exception: Low d-high minus high d-low, over low squared — subtraction order matters.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Derivative of the outside, keep the inside, times derivative of the inside.
exception: Must multiply by the inside derivative.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: sin → cos → −sin → −cos → sin.
exception: Missing negatives; degrees mode on calculators.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Raise the power by one, divide by the new power, and add C.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: LIATE: prefer u from Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential (earlier wins).
exception: Heuristic, not a theorem — some integrals need the opposite choice or cyclic methods.
reason: Useful if taught as guidance, not law.

phrase: If you see f(g(x))·g'(x), let u = g(x) (undo the chain rule).
exception: Watch constant factors. For definite integrals, change limits to u-values (or substitute back).
reason: Mathematically sound reverse-chain description.

phrase: Log asks: what power?
exception: Change-of-base errors; log of negative.
steps: log_b a = c means b^c = a
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Logs turn × into +, ÷ into −, and powers out front.
exception: log(xy)=log x+log y; log(x/y)=log x−log y; log(x^k)=k log x. No log(x+y) split. Arguments positive.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Differentiation and integration undo each other (Fundamental Theorem).
exception: Needs continuity hypotheses. +C for indefinite integrals. √(x²)=|x|. Limits matter for definite integrals.
reason: Directionally true but oversimplified.

phrase: Permutations when order matters; combinations when order does not.
exception: With/without replacement changes the count. Indistinguishable objects need different formulas.
reason: Correct high-value distinction.

phrase: For typical unimodal skew: mean-median-mode alphabetical for left skew; reverse-alphabetical for right skew.
exception: Often false (von Hippel and others): mean–median–mode order is not a reliable skewness rule.
steps: Prefer comparing mean to median, or use a plot / skewness statistic.
reason: Unreliable rule frequently taught as fact; unsafe as a trusted phrase.

phrase: A p-value is the chance, assuming the null is true, of data at least this extreme.
exception: p is not P(H₀ true). Small p suggests incompatibility with H₀ under the model — not proof. Avoid p-hacking.
reason: Definition correct; must block 'probability the null is true'.

phrase: Boxplot whiskers reach the furthest point within 1.5 × IQR of the quartiles; beyond that are outliers.
exception: Some software/curricula use different fences (or min/max whiskers). Check the convention.
reason: Tukey rule is standard but not universal.

phrase: Old MacDonald used chi-square: E, I, E, I, O.
reason: Letter mash does not map cleanly to Σ(O−E)²/E; teach the formula directly.

phrase: Each side over the sine of the angle it faces.
exception: Ambiguous case (SSA).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Pythagoras with a correction: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.
exception: Sign of cosine in obtuse triangles; wrong opposite side.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Half of two sides times the sine of the included angle.
exception: The angle must be included between the two sides.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: sin cos cos sin, sign stays. cos cos sin sin, sign swaps.
exception: Wrong sign patterns; tan formula separate.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Double the angle: sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A.
exception: Mixing cos double-angle forms.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: π is 180°. To radians × π/180; to degrees × 180/π.
exception: π rad = 180°. Multiply by π/180 for radians; by 180/π for degrees.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Lengths × k, areas × k², volumes × k³.
exception: Applying k to area directly.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: A diameter always sees a right angle.
exception: Using a non-diameter chord.
steps: Endpoint angle on diameter is right.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: A tangent meets the radius at a right angle.
exception: Confusing with alternate segment theorem.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: The center angle is double the rim angle (same arc).
exception: Same arc required. Center angle is twice the inscribed angle on that arc.
steps: ∠ at center = 2 × ∠ at circumference on same arc.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Opposite corners in a circle add to 180°.
exception: Applying to non-cyclic quads.
steps: Opposite angles of cyclic quad are supplementary.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: AP sum = n/2 × (first + last).
exception: Off-by-one in n; confusing AP with GP.
steps: Find n, first, last (or use 2a+(n−1)d form).
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Each term multiplies by the same ratio r.
exception: r negative; |r|<1 infinite sum conditions.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: A sector is a pizza slice: θ/360 of the whole circle.
exception: Mixing degrees and radians.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Elimination: make one letter match, then add or subtract to wipe it out.
exception: Adding when signs same; arithmetic slips.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.

phrase: Midpoint averages the coordinates. Distance is Pythagoras on the grid.
exception: Midpoint averages coordinates. Distance uses Pythagoras on Δx, Δy.
reason: Mathematically sound; already present in the app.
